lhs: Compute the grouped forward convolution using logical batch and spatial addresses in the requested output dimension order.
rhs: Bitcast input to a matrix, multiply its rows by a single weight, then bitcast rows to the requested output shape.
conditions: Rank three, one filter tap and one channel, same descending dense layouts with minor feature, unit groups/stride/dilations. With batch and spatial axes swapped, universal equality holds iff at least one of their extents is at most one. Matching axes always agree.
types: Exact Nat logical data; the witness is representable as U32.
overlap: A normalized convolution/dot with shared row order has a prior proof. The new criterion tests whether equal physical layout arrays enforce that row order and includes live mismatched dimensions.

lhs: Pointwise add of two separate one-update scatters.
rhs: Concat: apply the left reducer to both patches on the sum. Nested: update the sum with the right scatter and then the left.
conditions: Two distinct in-bounds positions in a common vector of length greater than two. Add reducer may read each of the two parameters twice, in either position. Universal preservation holds iff both reducers use both parameters.
types: Exact integer array payload; flags as declared for the two paths.
overlap: Historical ordinary-add combination and single-scatter duplicate-role failures precede this classification for two independently matched reducers. One refutation case with full role criterion; two exits counted together.

lhs: Initialize a rank-three padded window at +0 and sum all admitted entries.
rhs: Broadcast either the single covered original item or the already padded item, before or after F16-to-F32 widening.
conditions: Two frozen concrete static geometries, two nontrivial window dimensions, no dilation or reversal, all values zero with either sign.
types: F32 RNE and bitwise observation; F16 zero sign preserved on widening.
overlap: Prior negative-zero partial update and reduce results concern different expressions. Here the source guard selects combined or existing padding, in each operand type.
